characterization_methods: Laser detection of radius of curvature
evidence: Film composition was analyzed by Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) and hydrogen forward scattering spectroscopy using 50-nm-thick films. Spectroscopic ellipsometry and transmission electron spectroscopy (TEM) cross section measurements were used to determine film thickness. Film surface morphology was studied by atomic force microscopy (AFM). Film composition depth profiles were analyzed by secondary ion mass spectrometry. Chemical state analysis of the films was accomplished using x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). For electrical characterization a planar capacitor with phosphorus-implanted polysilicon electrode was fabricated or a mercury probe with a probe area of 7.2 cm2 was used to measure the C – V and I – V characteristics of films deposited on HF-last Si wafers. Film stress and thermal hysteresis were measured for 50-nm-thick films by change in wafer bow using laser detection of the radius of curvature during an anneal up to 900 °C with a ramp rate of 4 °C/min. Particle defects in the films were detected optically by light scattering measurements. Metal impurity analysis of the films was conducted using the HF vapor phase decomposition technique. Postdeposition anneal in N2 was conducted by rapid thermal processing in a hot-wall single-wafer system.
